title: Closed subschemes of a geometric fibre over a finite field are defined over a finite extension
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, with subfields $\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$. Let $X_0$ be a scheme of finite type over $k_0$, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $g_X=\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma):X\to X$ the geometric Frobenius automorphism of [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Let $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion. Then there are an integer $m\ge1$ and a closed subscheme $C_m\subseteq X_0\times_{k_0}\mathbf F_{q^m}$ whose base change along $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^m}$ is $i(C)$ as a closed subscheme of $X=(X_0\times_{k_0}\mathbf F_{q^m})\times_{\mathbf F_{q^m}}k$. Consequently there is an automorphism of schemes $\varphi:C\to C$ with $i\circ\varphi=g_X^m\circ i$.
The finite-type, closed-immersion and base-change notions are those of [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and [def-pc-base-change].

source.place: Final paragraph: finite coefficients and descent to one finite constant-field extension

proof.text: Put $K_n=\mathbf F_{q^n}\subset k$ for $n\ge1$, and order the positive integers by divisibility. By [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure], $K_n$ is exactly the root field of $T^{q^n}-T$. If $n\mid r$, iterating $x^{q^n}=x$ gives $x^{q^r}=x$, so $K_n\subseteq K_r$; $nr$ is a common upper bound of $n,r$. Every $b\in k$ is algebraic over $k_0$. Its minimal polynomial of degree $d\ge1$ identifies $k_0[b]$ with a field having a basis $1,b,\ldots,b^{d-1}$ and therefore $q^d$ elements. Uniqueness of the subfield with $q^d$ elements puts $b$ in $K_d$. Thus $k=\bigcup_{n\ge1}K_n$ as a directed union of rings. Its colimit property is explicit: compatible ring maps from the $K_n$ send $b$ to its image at any stage containing $b$; a common multiple makes this independent of the stage and preserves addition and multiplication.

source.place: Final paragraph, finite constant-field coefficients; elementary algebraic elaboration

proof.text: Set $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}K_n$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$. For $n\mid r$ the transition $S_r\to S_n$ is affine: its target has just the two opens $\varnothing,S_n$, whose inverse images are affine. The affine-limit clause of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] and Step 1 identify $S=\varprojlim_n S_n$. Each $S_n$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Thus this small directed inverse system satisfies exactly the base hypotheses of [thm-pd-spreading-out].

Write $X_n=X_0\times_{k_0}K_n$. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2), both $X_n\to S_n$ and $X\to S$ are of finite type. The affine closed-immersion description in [def-weil-closed-immersion] gives $i^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A)=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ over every affine open of $X$. A finite affine cover of $X$ by finite-type $k$-algebras therefore pulls back to a finite affine cover of $C$ by quotient algebras of finite type over $k$. Hence $C\to S$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. This retains the ideals themselves, including nilpotents, rather than replacing $C$ by its underlying closed set.

For a field $L$, $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is locally Noetherian, since its coordinate ring has only the ideals $(0),(1)$; it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. If $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is of finite type, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $Y$ locally Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes $Y$ quasi-separated. Its quasi-compact structure map and the quasi-compact base make $Y$ quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2); part (1) of that node makes the structure map quasi-separated. Finally [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes it locally of finite presentation. These three properties give finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Apply this argument to $X_0/k_0$, $X_n/K_n$, $X/k$ and $C/k$. In particular all these schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and all their structure maps are of finite presentation.

Apply clause (1) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to the finite-presentation map $C\to S$ over the inverse system of Step 2. It supplies an $n\ge1$, a finite-presentation $C_n\to S_n$, and an isomorphism $\epsilon_n:C\xrightarrow{\sim}C_n\times_{S_n}S$ over $S$. The target already has the model $X_n$. Base-change associativity identifies $X_n\times_{S_n}S$ with $X$, by [def-pc-base-change]. Clause (2) of [thm-pd-spreading-out], applied to the morphism $i\epsilon_n^{-1}$ between these two base changes, gives an $r$ divisible by $n$ and an $S_r$-morphism $i_r:C_r\to X_r$ whose base change is $i$ under the induced isomorphism $\epsilon_r$. Here $C_r=C_n\times_{S_n}S_r$. The structure maps of $C_r$ and $X_r$ remain of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), so their schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by part (2) and the affine base.

The map $i_r$ is locally of finite type. Indeed, take an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X_r$. Cover $C_r$ by finite-type affine $K_r$-charts, which exist because finite presentations are in particular finite sets of algebra generators. Cover the intersection of each chart with $i_r^{-1}(V)$ by principal opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Each $A$ remains of finite type over $K_r$: a principal localization adds one generator and the relation making it inverse to the localized element. Any finite list generating $A$ as a $K_r$-algebra also generates it as a $B$-algebra, since $K_r\to A$ factors through $B$. This is the affine criterion of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Step 4 makes $X_r$ locally Noetherian, so [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $i_r$ locally of finite presentation. The source $C_r$ and target $X_r$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $i_r$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Hence it is of finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

The morphism $i_r$ of Step 6 is of finite presentation between finite-presentation $S_r$-schemes, and its base change to $S$ is the given closed immersion $i$. Apply [lemma-nagata-closed-immersion-stage-exists] to this morphism and the system of Step 2. It supplies an $m$ divisible by $r$ such that $i_m:C_m\to X_m$ is a closed immersion. The descended isomorphism $\epsilon:C\xrightarrow{\sim}C_m\times_{K_m}k$ satisfies $(i_m\times\operatorname{id}_k)\epsilon=i$ by construction. Regard $C_m$ with $i_m$ as a closed subscheme of $X_m$. This proves precisely the asserted equality after base change as a closed subscheme, not merely equality of images on points. All indices are positive integers, so $m\ge1$.

The root description in [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure] says $b^{q^m}=b$ for $b\in K_m$. Thus arithmetic Frobenius to the $m$th power restricts to the identity on $K_m$, and so does its inverse $\gamma^m$. Consequently $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^m)$ is an automorphism over $S_m$. On $D=C_m\times_{K_m}k$ form $h=\operatorname{id}_{C_m}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^m)$ by [def-pc-base-change]; its inverse uses $\gamma^{-m}$. Define $\varphi=\epsilon^{-1}h\epsilon$. The two projections of the fibre product give $(i_m\times\operatorname{id}_k)h=(\operatorname{id}_{X_m}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^m))(i_m\times\operatorname{id}_k)$. Under $X_m\times_{K_m}k=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, the middle automorphism is $g_X^m$ by the explicit formula in [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Substitution of $(i_m\times\operatorname{id}_k)\epsilon=i$ gives $i\varphi=g_X^m i$. Thus $\varphi$ is the required scheme automorphism, semilinear over $k$; no claim that it is a $k$-morphism is needed.
